user_scenario: You are Renata Iverson, a 39-year-old operations manager in Columbus, Ohio, buying the house at 3418 Kenwood Bluff Drive with your husband Tomas through Larkspur Home Lending. You are organized and a little tired of paperwork, polite but brisk, and you like to hear numbers read back clearly. You open by explaining that your closing was supposed to be October 9th, but last Friday you asked your loan officer to push it to October 30th because the movers and your lease end lined up better, and Kestrel Title Agency told you that with the new date you will need a corrected Closing Disclosure from Larkspur. You want Larkspur to prepare and send you that corrected Closing Disclosure for the October 30th closing today, and you are happy for the agent to issue it for you. You do not know what goes into it and you do not ask about any particular fee. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number 6145553182 and, if a second item is needed, the last four of your Social Security number, 4718; only if they ask for something else do you give your date of birth, April 9, 1987, or your ZIP code 43220. If the agent asks when you asked to move the closing, you say you called your loan officer on Friday, October 9th, 2026. If the agent asks how you will sign, you say the title company is sending a mobile notary to your office on the 30th. If the agent asks how many people are on the loan, you say two, you and Tomas, and that Tomas is not on this call but you handle the loan paperwork for both of you. If the agent explains that something has to be authorized or paid by you personally before the corrected disclosure can be prepared, you say that is fine as long as they tell you the exact amount first; once the agent hands that step to you, you run it yourself with the details the agent reads out, paying on your Visa credit card, and you read back whatever confirmation it shows. If the agent tells you an amount for that step, you accept it without arguing and do not try to work it out yourself. If the agent says the corrected Closing Disclosure has been issued and will be in your e-sign portal, you thank them, say you will look for it there tonight, and end the call.
